desc: Implement a brute-force BFS over configuration graph for N ≤ ~8 to serve as oracle for testing.
Work out by hand the exact minimal swap maneuver cost on small gadgets (triangle, star/branch vertex, path-with-leaf, cycle of length k) to understand the "passing" overhead precisely.
Hypothesize formula (two internally-disjoint paths sum / tree parking 2d+2ℓ) and refute the "impossible iff graph is a path" conjecture via the leaf-behind-S counterexample.

Write an enumerative tester generating all small connected graphs (N ≤ 6, edges ≤ 9) and all S≠T, comparing formula vs oracle; it exposed systematic mismatches (endpoint parking, parking-side condition, ℓ > 1, disjointness too strict).

Run tester, collect concrete counterexamples, and refine formula: endpoint/side-aware parking with true off-path ℓ via BFS, cycle case as d + shortest S–T path avoiding internal vertices of shortest path; iterate until zero mismatches on N ≤ 6 and random N ≤ 8.
Derive efficient O(N+M) or O((N+M) log N) algorithm from validated formula (block-cut tree / biconnected components, BFS distances, min off-path branch distance along S–T path).
Finalize production solution with fast I/O (sys.stdin.buffer), adjacency lists, print -1 when impossible.
